messages:
Anna (Support): Heads-up: multiple paying customers are reporting intermittent 502/504s to the hosted /v1/generate endpoint since ~09:22 UTC. Started small, now ~8% of requests failing for one tenant. Customer provided curl + x-request-id. Escalating to eng-sre and runtime.

Anna (Support): Sample repro from customer (redacted API key):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.5","input":"hello"}' 
```
Response: 502 Bad Gateway, body: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers". X-Request-ID: rq_0a1b2c3d.

Sofia (Customer Success): Affected customers: three different accounts in prod (eu-west-1 and us-east-1 regions). One customer reported 504s after 30s, others 502 immediate. They say it started after a burst of requests from a new internal job.

Jared (Eng-SRE): Looking at edge metrics now. I'm seeing a spike in envoy cluster.rq_error for cluster "hosted-api-upstream-default" starting at 09:21:30 UTC. Concurrency at edge jumped ~3x.

Jared (Eng-SRE): Envoy logs for one instance show repeated: `upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers` and `HTTP/1.1 504 upstream request timeout` interleaved. Pasting snippet: 
```
[09:22:11] ERR envoy upstream connect error: connection reset by peer, upstream_host:10.0.12.45:8080, x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d
[09:22:40] WARN envoy upstream request timeout: route "/v1/generate", upstream cluster hosted-api-upstream-default
```

Priya (Eng-Runtime): Could be two buckets: (A) upstream inference workers are overloaded and closing connections; (B) a load-balancer or envoy connection pool exhaustion. I pushed a query to the runtime metrics (kv cache hit ratio, worker free slots). Runtime shows worker queue length spike and several OOM kills on a single instance around 09:21:50 (likely model process crash) — but need container logs.

Marco (Infra): I'm checking the LB / nginx side. No config changes. NGINX metrics show many TCP RSTs to backend pool 10.0.12.0/24. Healthchecks stayed green. Could be abrupt upstream process termination. Also seeing short bursts of client-side keepalive closure.

Anna (Support): Customer is asking for ETA and mitigation. They said 80% of their calls succeed but important tail is failing.

Jared (Eng-SRE): Priorities: 1) Collect backend container logs for the affected hosts 10.0.12.45/46; 2) Check coredumps / OOM events; 3) Verify envoy connection pool saturation and CDS/EDS churn; 4) Provide mitigation (route traffic away or scale).

Priya (Eng-Runtime): I grabbed logs from runtime host 10.0.12.45: process supervisor shows restart loops: `worker_main exited with code 137` (OOM). Model memory footprint increased due to some customers trying long sequences. In one log: 
```
2026-03-15T09:21:48Z worker_main[pid=4211]: Allocation failed, OOM, killing process
2026-03-15T09:21:49Z supervisor: restarting worker_main
```
This explains connect resets -> envoy sees upstream suddenly gone -> 502. If the worker is slow to restart, gateway will surface 504s.

Marco (Infra): Confirmed: kernel dmesg on that host shows multiple `Out of memory: Kill process` events at 09:21:48. Host memory is 384GB; a single model run pinned a lot of GPU RAM and spilled to host memory due to swap config.

Jared (Eng-SRE): Short-term mitigations: 1) Add a temporary route-weight to steer traffic away from the affected pool (set route weight to 0 for cluster host 10.0.12.*) 2) Increase envoy upstream_connect_timeout? That won't fix OOMs but reduces immediate 502s. 3) Scale up the capacity group (add two more runtime nodes) and mark unhealthy hosts out.

Priya (Eng-Runtime): I can push a slot-limiter patch to reject single requests that exceed a configured seq_length threshold (reject with 4xx) but that's code change and risky. Instead I'd propose quickly applying a per-request max_sequence enforcement at the sidecar/proxy layer to drop obvious abusers.

Marco (Infra): I've initiated a graceful drain of host 10.0.12.45 and 10.0.12.46. Also increased the autoscaler threshold for the pool to add two nodes immediately. Draining should help envoy stop routing to OOMing hosts.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued: autoscaler/increase-pool-size v1.2. Starting rollout to infra-autoscaler service.

Jared (Eng-SRE): After drain started at 09:25:10, edge error rate dropped from 8% to 1.2% over ~2m. We'll keep an eye on tail latency and any remaining 504s.

Anna (Support): Passed the mitigation note to customers: we are draining bad hosts and scaling pool; suggested temporary retry with exponential backoff. Customers appreciated ETA.

Sofia (Customer Success): Two customers requested logs/export for their request IDs. Jared / Priya, can we produce per-request debug bundle for rq_0a1b2c3d and rq_4f5g6h7i?

Priya (Eng-Runtime): I collected traces for both request IDs. Trace shows request arrived at edge, proxied to 10.0.12.45, then worker OOM'd while allocating KV cache for prefix. I'll upload sanitized bundles to the secure bucket and link here.

Priya (Eng-Runtime): Link: https://s3.redwood.ai/debug-bundles/1912345678-rq_0a1b2c3d.tar.gz (internal). Contains envoy access logs, runtime stdout, and dmesg.

Jared (Eng-SRE): Postmortem notes (short): root cause = single request pattern triggered an anomalously large memory allocation on the runtime host -> OOM -> worker killed -> envoy observed abrupt upstream disconnects -> edge surfaced 502s/504s. Contributing factors: no per-request hard-limit on sequence length, pool autoscaler lag, lack of early rejection at edge.

Anna (Support): Customers want assurance this won't reoccur. Can we add follow-ups: 1) enforce per-request seq limit at edge (short-term); 2) tune autoscaler and warm pool for bursts; 3) add clearer 5xx semantics when upstream OOM vs transient LB issues; 4) run load test for long-seq scenarios.

Priya (Eng-Runtime): Agreed. I'll open a runtime ticket to add quick reject at sidecar, and a medium-term runtime change to pre-check memory before dispatching heavy sequences.

Marco (Infra): I'll work on autoscaler policy changes and healthcheck aggressiveness so we detect flapping hosts sooner.

Jared (Eng-SRE): I'll draft an incident follow-up with timeline and customer impact metrics (p95 errors, affected tenants). Will attach debug bundle and mitigation steps.

Anna (Support): Thank you all. Customer-facing summary sent at 09:35 UTC. Will update thread after postmortem published.

Sofia (Customer Success): Customer reply: "Thanks — the mitigation helped. Please let us know when this is fixed long-term." :thumbsup:

Anna (Support): Closing internal thread once postmortem PR is merged.
